query: Analyze the global ocean dissolved oxygen inventory over 2000–2020 to determine how it has changed over time. The analysis should account for seasonal variability and assess the magnitude and statistical significance of the long-term trend. Results should be summarized using an appropriate time-series visualization.

Characterize the global occurrence of oxygen minimum zones over 2010–2020 by examining the spatial distribution and vertical extent of low-oxygen waters. Assess how the thickness of hypoxic layers varies across different regions of the global ocean, and present the results in a spatially explicit visualization.

Analyze the spatial variability of nitrogen-to-phosphorus (N:P) stoichiometry across the major ocean basins (Southern Ocean, Arctic Ocean, Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean) during January over the period 1975–1985. Characterize how N:P ratios differ among basins in the upper ocean and assess the statistical distribution of these stoichiometric signatures across regions. Summarize the results using a basin-scale comparative box plots.

How do phosphate anomalies in the upper equatorial Pacific (0-100 m) evolve in space and time from 1995 to 2000? Assess how seasonal anomalies organize and evolve zonally across the basin, and summarize the dominant seasonal patterns in nutrient dynamics using an appropriate time–longitude representation.

Analyze long-term ENSO variability over 1960–2020 using the Niño 3.4 index. Examine the temporal structure and amplitude of interannual variability, and determine when major warm and cold ENSO events occurred. Present the results in a time-series visualization that distinguishes background variability from extreme phases.

Characterize the monthly climatological seasonal cycle of surface salinity in the Indian Ocean over the period 1990–2020, focusing on the upper ocean (0–50 m). Describe the amplitude and phasing of the seasonal salinity variability, and explain how monsoonal processes shape the observed monthly patterns across the basin.
